# Davy Keith

## Overview

- **Age:** Nine years old (at the end of Volume 3)  <sub>[v2 c1 P31](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0031), [v2 c10 P47](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0047), [v2 c10 P86](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0086), [v3 c28 P5](../source/v03-c28.md#nw-v03-c28-p0005)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P33](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0033)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v3 c39 P0](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0000)</sub>
- **Origin:** East Grafton, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v2 c1 P29](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0029), [v2 c8 P0](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolboy  <sub>[v2 c21 P0](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Davy is a handsome, chubby boy with a crop of fuzzy yellow ringlets all over his round head and roguish, dancing hazel eyes. He has a snub nose, a cheerful smile, and a single dimple in one cheek that gives him a comical, lopsided look when he laughs. As he grows older, he becomes tall and sturdy, eventually losing a front tooth in his school years.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P33](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0033), [v2 c8 P2](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0002), [v2 c8 P25](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0025), [v2 c20 P9](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0009), [v2 c22 P18](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0018), [v3 c22 P18](../source/v03-c22.md#nw-v03-c22-p0018)_

## Personality

Davy is an energetic, inquisitive, and irrepressible boy who is constantly getting into mischief due to his restless nature and love of fun. He possesses an insatiable curiosity about the world and is notorious for asking endless questions about everything. Though prone to disobedience, telling wild tales, and engaging in naughty pranks, he has a warm, affectionate heart and a knack for winning people's love. He is fiercely protective of his twin sister Dora despite teasing her, and he holds a deep, loyal affection for Anne.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P33](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0033), [v2 c7 P30](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0030), [v2 c8 P2](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0002), [v2 c8 P8](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0008), [v2 c8 P25](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0025), [v2 c8 P54](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0054), [v2 c9 P21](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0021), [v2 c10 P87](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0087), [v2 c10 P89](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0089), [v2 c20 P8](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0008)_

## History

Davy Keith and his twin sister, Dora, were left orphans at the age of six when their mother, Mary Keith, died of a lingering illness in East Grafton. Because their uncle in British Columbia could not immediately care for them, Marilla Cuthbert took the twins into Green Gables. Davy quickly established a reputation for endless antics, such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck in church, trapping his sister Dora in a toolhouse, putting a toad in Marilla's bed, and chasing Mrs. Lynde's rooster to death. Despite his frequent misbehavior and knack for telling wild stories, Anne Shirley took a gentle approach to his discipline, earning his deep devotion and gradually helping him learn right from wrong. Following the death of his uncle Richard, who left a trust fund for the twins, Davy and Dora became permanent residents of Green Gables. As he grew older, Davy attended Avonlea school, befriended boys like Milty Boulter, and slowly matured into a handsome, albeit still lively and inquisitive, schoolboy.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P29](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0029), [v2 c1 P33](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0033), [v2 c7 P33](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0033), [v2 c8 P37](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0037), [v2 c8 P49](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0049), [v2 c8 P61](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0061), [v2 c10 P38](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0038), [v2 c10 P52](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0052), [v2 c21 P0](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0000), [v2 c22 P22](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0022), [v3 c10 P17](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0017), [v3 c13 P38](../source/v03-c13.md#nw-v03-c13-p0038)_

## Background by volume

- Orphaned at the age of six when his sick mother, Mary Keith, passed away  <sub>[v2 c1 P31](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0031), [v2 c1 P33](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0033), [v2 c7 P23](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0023)</sub>

> You're awful nice, Anne. Milty Boulter wrote on his slate today and showed it to Jennie Sloane, 'Roses red and vi'lets blue, Sugar's sweet, and so are you' and that 'spresses my feelings for you ezackly, Anne.  <sub>[v2 c25 P73](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0073)</sub>

> Anne, don't you like me a little bit, even if I ain't a good boy like Paul?  <sub>[v2 c8 P54](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0054)</sub>

One was a good deal bigger than the other and Marilla didn't say which was mine. But I give the biggest piece to Dora. That was good of me, wasn't it?  <sub>[v2 c19 P48](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0048)</sub>
